_about: Field terms for F675, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

known-answer-test.definition: a test of a method on a case where the true answer is fixed by physics or by construction, so that any wrong reading is a fault of the method
known-answer-test.excludes: agreement with another method, which can share the same fault

granger.definition: a regression test of whether the past values of one series improve the prediction of another beyond that series' own past; here an F test on lags 1 and 2
granger.excludes: a test of same-year effects, and proof of a physical cause

panel.definition: a set of units, here tree-ring sites, each observed over time and analysed together so that one statistic summarises all of them
panel.excludes: a verdict reached site by site, and a pooled regression that treats all years of all sites as one series

direction-index.definition: the mean over sites of d, the z-score of the climate-to-ring Granger test minus that of the ring-to-climate test; positive values point from summer temperature to ring width
direction-index.excludes: a test of significance at any one site

z-score.definition: the point of the standard normal distribution that leaves the p value above it, so that a smaller p gives a larger z; here capped at 6
z-score.excludes: a standardised value of the data themselves

high-pass.definition: a filter that keeps fast variation and removes slow trends; here each series minus a Gaussian smooth of width 10 years, then scaled to unit variance
high-pass.excludes: first differences, which are reported as a separate arm

first-difference.definition: each year's value minus the previous year's, a second way to remove slow trends that weights the fastest changes most
first-difference.excludes: the high-pass filter, which removes trends by smoothing

iaaft.definition: a copy of a series built by repeated rounds of Fourier phase randomisation and rank reordering, so that it keeps both the original spectrum, and with it the autocorrelation, and the original set of values, while its timing against any other series is lost
iaaft.excludes: a shuffle of single years, which destroys the autocorrelation

detection-rate.definition: the share of sites at which the Granger test in one direction gives p 0.05 or below; for synthetic worlds it is averaged over the draws
detection-rate.excludes: a rate corrected for testing 161 sites

direction-accuracy.definition: the share of sites at which the sign of d matches the direction planted in a synthetic world; 0.5 is what a coin would give
direction-accuracy.excludes: whether the test at any site is significant

block-bootstrap.definition: an interval made by resampling whole 2 degree blocks of sites with replacement, here 2,000 times, so that neighbouring sites that share climate move together and the interval is not too narrow
block-bootstrap.excludes: a bootstrap over single sites, and a binomial interval that treats sites as independent

site-pairing.definition: a control in which each ring series is paired with the summer temperature of a random site at least 1,000 km away, so that real coupling is removed while both series keep their own form; repeated 199 times
site-pairing.excludes: pairings with nearby sites, which share regional climate

time-reversal.definition: the same test run on both series read backwards in time; a method that reads direction from lag order should flip

gating-check.definition: a preregistered rule on a synthetic world that the instrument must pass before any reading of the real data counts; under the kill condition a single failure removes all standing
gating-check.excludes: power checks and limit checks, which were recorded but could not remove standing

benjamini-hochberg.definition: a rule that adjusts a set of p values so that, among the tests called significant, the expected share of false calls stays at or below a chosen rate, here 0.05; the adjusted value is called q
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: the stricter Bonferroni rule, which bounds the chance of any false call

prior-summer.definition: the slope on the previous year's summer temperature in a regression of this year's ring width on this year's and last year's summer temperature
prior-summer.excludes: the same-year slope, and any effect of the ring's own past unless it is added to the regression
